# routeros_port (Resource)




<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the serial port, for example `serial0`. On the first apply the port with this name must already exist on the router; afterwards the port is tracked by its internal identifier and changing the name renames the port.

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `baud_rate` (String) Speed of the port in bits per second, or `auto` to detect it automatically, for example `115200`.
- `data_bits` (Number) Number of data bits per character. Use `7` for ASCII data and `8` for binary data.
- `dtr` (String) State of the RS-232 DTR signal circuit used by hardware flow control.
> RouterOS does not report this property back in `/port/print`, so its value is kept from the configuration and cannot be refreshed from the device.
- `flow_control` (String) Method used to pause and resume the transmission.
- `parity` (String) Parity bit used for error detection.
- `rts` (String) State of the RS-232 RTS signal circuit used by hardware flow control.
> RouterOS does not report this property back in `/port/print`, so its value is kept from the configuration and cannot be refreshed from the device.
- `stop_bits` (Number) Number of stop bits that follow every character.

### Read-Only

- `channels` (Number) Number of channels the port provides.
- `device` (String) Name of the device that provides this port, for USB serial adapters.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `inactive` (Boolean)
- `line_state` (String) Comma separated list of the RS-232 signal lines that are currently asserted.
- `used_by` (String) Service that currently holds the port, for example `Serial Console(#0)`.
